items.title: Extract command schema and ToolDef definitions
items.context: Move reusable schema/type definitions out of cli-engine.ts into a CLI module without changing validation semantics or exported compatibility names.

happy.desc: ToolDef and schema-only command definitions are moved into CLI catalog/schema modules while cli-engine.ts still exports MAIN_TOOLS and ToolDef for existing consumers.

edge.desc: Zod schema descriptions, enums, required/optional flags, defaults, and nested object/array help metadata remain behaviorally identical for representative commands.

adversarial.desc: No flag parsing, alias resolution, owner lease gate, lifecycle dispatch, handler registration, or Authority receipt behavior is moved or changed by this story.

items.userSees: `lattice story_create --help` still prints the same story_create arguments, and MAIN_TOOLS remains importable from cli-engine.ts while schema definitions live in cli modules.

items.title: Extract MAIN_TOOLS command catalog assembly
items.context: Move the large command list and tool map construction into a dedicated module that cli-engine.ts imports, keeping existing command ids, aliases, owners, and policies unchanged.

happy.desc: MAIN_TOOLS assembly lives outside cli-engine.ts and exposes the same command-name set and ordering as before the extraction.

edge.desc: Third-party extraTools still append to the runtime TOOLS list and main built-ins still win command lookup ordering.

adversarial.desc: No command disappears, duplicates unexpectedly, or changes from current host semantics; Gemini is not reintroduced as a current host by catalog text.

items.userSees: `lattice help` still lists the same command set and ordering, while cli-engine.ts no longer contains the inline MAIN_TOOLS catalog block.

items.title: Verify command catalog behavior and contracts
items.context: Run build and focused command contract checks proving command registration, JSON stdout behavior, and public compatibility exports did not drift.

happy.desc: Focused command catalog smoke passes and proves representative commands remain visible through MAIN_TOOLS and help output.

edge.desc: Project build and process fact contract still pass after catalog extraction.

adversarial.desc: The smoke fails if representative help output loses command names, required markers, dry-run/owner lease guidance, or Lattice branding due to catalog extraction.

items.userSees: `npm --prefix packages/main run test:command-catalog-smoke` prints a passing command catalog smoke after build and contract checks.
